newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot electricity off on soft demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot electricity off on soft demand.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. fell Friday on soft demand due to the onset of cooler-than-normal weather, market sources said.
"It's ridiculously cool," said one Houston trader.

Weak spot demand overrode concerns about reduced generation capacity tied to ongoing outages of New York Power Authority's 780 megawatt (MW) Fitzpatrick nuclear station and Boston Edison Co's 670 Pilgrim nuclear plant.

In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), non-firm weekend electricity prices for heavy load hours were quoted at $16.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) for the western part of the state, down from Thursday's prices for Friday delivery near $18.50.
Weekend, peak prices in the eastern part of the NYPP district were pegged near $22.00, off from Thursday's $23.00 for Friday delivery.
Non-firm weekend NYPP for light load hours in western New York was assessed at $13.00 and eastern New York $16.00, compared with Thursday's range of $15.00-$16.00.
On Monday, western NYPP peak electricity was discussed in the $18.00 area and eastern NYPP near $20.00.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), non-firm, peak electricity delivered to the Northeast Utilities (NU) territory border during the weekend was quoted at $22.75-$23.25 compared with Thursday's $25.00.
Off-peak weekend electricity to the NU border was assessed at $18.00, down from Thursday's $19.00-$20.00 range.
On Monday, peak, non-firm NEPOOL prices was pegged at $27.25-$27.75, and off-peak, non-firm values at $19.00-$20.00.
New York Power Authority today said it planned for Fitzpatrick 1 to start power production over the weekend after being tripped off line Monday.
Boston Edison Co's Pilgrim plant was expected to be shut until earlier next week to correct problems with a set of the plant's heat exchangers.
